request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: DNA_damage activates Cdc2_CycB   (1 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC2829054 (p53-deficient cells with wild type Cdk2): "As expected, p53-deficient cells normally induced Cdk1Y15-P after IR (Figure 4B); in contrast, the levels of Cdk1Y15-P did not increase after IR in cells that were also Cdk2-deficient."

NODE TO CHANGE: Cdc2_CycB
CURRENT RULE:   Cdc2_CycB, Cdc25 & !Wee1 & !PTEN & !p21
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): Cdc2_CycB, (Cdc25 & !Wee1 & !PTEN & !p21) | DNA_damage

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- V02 (Section 3.2, damage: the four stable fates); setting {'DNA_damage': 1}: g2_arrest; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 1, 'Wee1': 1, 'PTEN': 1, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0}
- V08 (Table 1 rows 1 and 4, p53 E1 + PTEN KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'PTEN': 0}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['apoptosis']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 1, 'Wee1': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1}

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- DNA_damage must be able to switch Cdc2_CycB on and never off: it acts on Cdc2_CycB only in the direction 'activates'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use Cdc2_CycB in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "Conditioned the claimed activation on !p53. Evidence context is p53-deficient cells with wild-type Cdk2, so the DNA_damage effect should apply when p53 is absent. Both counterexamples have p53=1 (V02 witness with p21=1/Wee1=1/PTEN=1/Cdc25=0, V08 witness with p53=1/PTEN=0) where Cdc2_CycB must stay 0 to preserve arrest/senescence. Adding & !p53 blocks the spurious DNA_damage| term there, while DNA_damage can still turn Cdc2 on when base is 0 and p53=0, keeping DNA_damage a pure activator and preserving base influences when DNA_damage=0 or p53=1.", "give_up": false, "rule": "(Cdc25 & !Wee1 & !PTEN & !p21) | (DNA_damage & !p53)"}
